message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of key points you’ll want to know about Texas traffic laws: | Topic | What You Need to Know | |-------|----------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45–65 mph on urban freeways).
• “No‑limit” highways allow speeds up to 85 mph, but only if conditions permit and you’re driving a vehicle capable of safe travel at those speeds. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety Seat Laws** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a federally approved child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Handheld phone use while driving is illegal for all drivers.
• Texting is prohibited for all drivers. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal for most drivers.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04%.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory education programs, and possible jail time. | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Running red lights or stop signs is a moving violation.
• Points are added to your driver record; accumulating points leads to license suspension. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles approaching from the right have priority.
• Pedestrians always have the right of way when crossing marked crosswalks. | | **Parking Regulations** | • Parking on sidewalks, in front of fire hydrants, or within 20 feet of a driveway is prohibited.
• In many cities, parking meters or permits may be required during business hours. | | **Vehicle Equipment Requirements** | • Headlights must be used between sunset and sunrise, and during inclement weather.
• Tires must have adequate tread depth (minimum 2 / 32 in for passenger cars). | | **Points System** | • Most moving violations add points to your Texas Driver Record.
• 6 points in 12 months triggers a 90‑day license suspension.
• 9 points in 24 months triggers a 180‑day suspension. | | **Common Traffic Tickets** | • Speeding, failure to yield, improper lane changes, and reckless driving are among the most frequent infractions. | ### How to Find Specific Statutes If you’d like to look up the exact legal text, you can check the Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 1). Many local municipalities also publish their own ordinances online—search “[city name] traffic ordinance” for city‑specific rules. Let me know if you’d like details on a particular rule, how to contest a ticket, or anything else!
